subject: Weird normalization plots from DIA-NN experiments

messages.author: 92c1f4710b7f5e5b
messages.subject: Weird normalization plots from DIA-NN experiments
parts:
Hi,

I wanted to see the effect of normalization on the data, so I ran dataProcess with normalization = "equalizeMedians''. Then, using "FeatureLevelData", I plotted a boxplot of the "ABUNDANCE" for each sample. I've used this approach before for DDA samples, and all went well. However, the boxplot looked a bit weird when I did this for DIA-NN data. A bunch of points equal to 0 were skewing the plots. My understanding is that this is intentional, as dataProcess converts to 1 all numbers that are zero or less than 1. Since ABUNDANCE is log2 transformed, the "1" intensity shows up as "0" in the abundance boxplot.

Going a little deeper, it seems MsstatsConvert is taking intensity values from "Fragment.Quant.Corrected" (report file from DIA-NN), and this is where some fragments are equal to zero. Hence, my questions:
1) What is the advantage of using/setting fragment values from zero to 1?
2) Why not replace the zero values with NA?

Here is one plot as an example:


Here are my dataProcess parameters:

maxquant.proposed <- dataProcess(diann.msstats, 
                                      normalization = "equalizeMedians",
                                      summaryMethod="TMP",
                                      censoredInt = "NA",
                                      MBimpute= FALSE,
                                      maxQuantileforCensored = 0.999)

Here is my ggplot code:
features_norm <- ggplot(data = maxquant.proposed$FeatureLevelData, mapping = aes(x = SUBJECT, y = ABUNDANCE, color = GROUP)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_blank()) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1");features_norm

Best,
Luiz

messages.author: 5c6e92c10ef28984
messages.subject: Re: Weird normalization plots from DIA-NN experiments
parts:
Hi,

we replace values of intensity between 0 and 1 with 1 before taking log transformation to make them equal to 0 (as a reasonable value), similarly, small log-intensities come from small intensities.
MSstats uses 0 and NA to differentiate between two sources of missingness (which is not reported by all data processing tools, but DIA-NN provides this information).
NA denotes values which we assume to be missing by random.
0 denotes values which we assume to be missing due to low abundance.
You can find more information about this in our MSstats 4.0 paper.

We've seen similar pattern in some other DIA data sets, I will get back to you after we discuss this again internally.

Kind regards,
Mateusz

messages.author: 92c1f4710b7f5e5b
messages.subject: Re: Weird normalization plots from DIA-NN experiments
parts:
Hi Mateusz,

Thank you for taking this topic for further discussion with your group. I appreciate it.

I wonder how this could affect the normalization and summarization. I assume it won't affect much, as I am using "equalizeMedians" and "TMP", which should be robust to these outliers.

Another thought is the possibility of taking the lowest intensity value of the experiment as the low abundance replacement. Or half the lowest intensity, which I had seen before in other approaches as well.
For full disclosure, I don't have strong mathematical skills to be giving advice, but it is just that the zero (or one) seems much of a contrast to the rest of the abundance values.

Looking forward to new opinions on this. In the meantime, I will find more details in the 4.0 paper.

Best,
Luiz
